steps.note: The cheese is ground and mixed with water.

steps.what: water and salts that bind calcium
steps.note: The mix is kept at 25–45 % solids, with phosphates, such as disodium phosphate, which bind the cheese's calcium so the fat emulsifies.
The mix is held hot, in studies from 80 °C for 1–10 minutes to 85 °C for 45 seconds, and kept below 85 °C where possible so less flavour is lost.
The hot mix is passed through a sieve, which leaves the undissolved cheese behind.
The mix is spray-dried, often in two stages, into a soluble powder; in a lab-scale dryer, the air goes in at 174 °C and out at 68 °C.

links.name: Deshwal et al. (2024), A Review on the Production and Characteristics of Cheese Powders, Foods 13, 2204

sources.text: The steps of a cheese emulsion and its spray-drying and the ranges quoted from the studies the review lists; the review gives no single standard.
